Om de site te verbeteren meten we zelf h: To improve the site, we measure how pages are used ourselves: which pages you view, which buttons and links you click (the visible text and the link address), how far you scroll, whether you start and submit a form, and how long you are active on a page. We don’t place cookies for this; we use a random code that applies only within one tab and disappears as soon as you close it. We don’t store IP addresses or browser details in these measurement data (only whether it’s a phone, tablet, or computer), and never what you enter in a form. We don’t share this measurement data with Google or other parties, use it to track you across other websites, or link it to your name. We also remember where you came from for each visit, for example a LinkedIn post or a search engine. If you book a conversation through our site in Calendly, we pass that tab code and the page to Calendly so we can see which page led to a conversation; our measurement data does not include a name or email address for this. The data is held by our processor Supabase on servers in Frankfurt and is deleted after 13 months. Because this measurement has little or no impact on your privacy, we don’t ask for your consent. Don’t want this measurement either? Turn on ‘Do Not Track’ or ‘Global Privacy Control’ in your browser; then we won’t measure anything.
